why: The student doesn't give the output (1 4 7 10) or say when the loop stops (after i=10, because isDone becomes true). The only claim is that `isDone = (i % 5 == 0);` is equivalent to the if. That is true here, because isDone starts false and the loop ends once it becomes true. But the student gives no reasoning or values to support it, so it counts as one correct, unjustified statement.
